name: Thailand: Bangkok, Chiang Mai and the islands

destination.name: Thailand: Bangkok, Chiang Mai and the islands
destination.pitch: Four nights in Bangkok for the river temples and Bib Gourmand noodles, then a coast picked by the calendar: Ao Nang, Railay and Lanta from November to April, Samui outside October to December, Chiang Mai for Lanna temples.

because.nature: Four Islands by longtail from Ao Nang, Ko Rok from Lanta between November and mid-May, Ang Thong's 42 limestone islands from Samui, and Doi Inthanon at 2,565m.
because.exploration: Wat Umong's tunnels, Susan Hoi's fossil shells, Old Town Lanta's stilt houses, Samui's Secret Buddha Garden and the Sunday Walking Street in Chiang Mai.
because.food: Jay Fai's crab omelette, Thipsamai pad thai, black pepper crab at Krua Apsorn, khao soi at Mae Sai, then oysters at Krua Thara, fish-farm tables at Sang Ga U and a class at Time for Lime.
because.relaxation: Khlong Nin and Kantiang on Lanta, hammocks over the water at Tew Lay on Railay East, Beach Republic's pool on Lamai, and Bophut's lane of restaurants.
because.culture: The Emerald Buddha, Wat Pho's Reclining Buddha and Wat Arun in Bangkok, then Wat Chiang Man, Phra Singh's Lanna murals and Monk Chat at Chedi Luang. The islands add little here.
because.adventure: Thaiwand Wall and deep-water solo off Railay, the ropes up to Diamond Cave and Princess Lagoon, and 1,260 steps up Tiger Cave Temple at 07:00.
because.city: The orange-flag boat on the Chao Phraya, Talat Noi's machine-shop alleys, Lumphini at dawn, Chatuchak on a weekend and Sky Bar at sunset.

destination.caveat: The coasts rain at opposite times: Andaman boats cancel May to October and Ko Rok shuts 16 May to 31 October, while Samui is wettest October to December. Bangkok is hottest March to May, Chiang Mai smokes in March and April, and island pins are approximate. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Bangkok
cities.base: Charoenkrung and Silom by the river: BTS Saphan Taksin at the pier, 10 to 15 minutes by boat or tuk-tuk to the Old City temples, and the train to Sukhumvit.

cities.name: Chiang Mai
cities.base: Inside the moat or just east of it by Tha Phae Gate: walk to the Old City temples and the Sunday Walking Street, 10 to 15 minutes by tuk-tuk to Nimman.

cities.name: Krabi
cities.base: Ao Nang, the beach strip 20 minutes from Krabi Town: a walkable restaurant row, the longtail pier for the islands, and range for Tiger Cave and the Emerald Pool.

cities.name: Railay
cities.base: Railay West, the sunset side, a short walk to Phra Nang. Boat only, 15 to 20 minutes from Ao Nang, and no boats after dark or in rough seas.

cities.name: Koh Lanta
cities.base: Khlong Dao or Khlong Nin on the west coast, for calm swimming and the restaurants; the beach you pick decides how much you walk. Old Town for atmosphere over sand.

cities.name: Koh Samui
cities.base: Bophut's Fisherman's Village on the north coast: a walkable lane of restaurants and the Friday walking street, without Chaweng's high-rises.

outings.name: Ko Rok and the Mu Ko Lanta islands
outings.why: A speedboat day to the outer islands of a 134 sq km park, with the Laem Tanod lighthouse on the Lanta tip as the land half. The islands shut every year from 16 May to 31 October.
outings.fallback: Old Town, Krua Lanta Yai and Big Tree Beer Garden on the east coast.

outings.name: Ang Thong National Marine Park
outings.why: 42 limestone islands 28km out with inland marine lakes, by authorised tour boat only; park fee 25 to 300 baht plus the boat.
outings.fallback: Na Muang Waterfalls and the Secret Buddha Garden, same inland detour.

outings.name: Ko Phi Phi Don and Maya Bay
outings.why: About an hour by speedboat to Phi Phi Don, with a Maya Bay stop capped at one hour, no swimming and 2,000 people a day. Rough seas May to October cancel boats.
outings.fallback: Four Islands by longtail from Ao Nang beach, or Tiger Cave Temple at 07:00.

outings.name: Doi Inthanon
outings.why: Thailand's highest point at 2,565m, about 60km out: Mae Klang, Wachirathan and Siriphum falls and the twin royal chedis. September is the wettest month and the trails get slick.
outings.fallback: Wat Umong and Wat Suan Dok at the foot of Doi Suthep.

places.name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
places.note: The late-18th-century royal compound, with the 66cm jade Emerald Buddha in Wat Phra Kaew. Shoulders and knees covered and no sandals, checked at the gate; be there at 08:30, ahead of the tour buses and the midday heat.

places.name: Wat Pho
places.neighborhood: Rattanakosin, next to the Grand Palace
places.note: The 46m gold-leafed Reclining Buddha, soles inlaid with mother-of-pearl, and the school where Thai massage is taught. Book a 30 to 60 minute massage on site after the Grand Palace; it is open three hours later than its neighbour.

places.name: Wat Arun
places.neighborhood: Thonburi, west bank of the Chao Phraya
places.note: An 82m prang faced in broken porcelain, 200 baht for foreigners. Cross on the 4 baht ferry from Tha Tien pier, climb the steep steps, then watch it at sunset from the east bank.

places.name: Wat Saket (Golden Mount)
places.note: About 300 steps up a man-made hill to one of the few clear views over the Old City's rooftops and spires. Half the crowd of the palace circuit; go late afternoon and walk to Fai Ta Lu for dinner.

places.name: Jim Thompson House
places.note: Six teak houses put together on a canal by the American silk man who vanished in the Cameron Highlands in 1967 and was never found. Guided tour only, included in the ticket.

places.name: Museum Siam
places.note: Fourteen hands-on rooms on what it means to be Thai, built as much for Thai school groups as for visitors. The best counterweight to the temples and air-conditioned for the midday hours; closed Mondays.

places.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
places.neighborhood: Chatuchak, north Bangkok, on the BTS and MRT
places.note: Over 15,000 stalls in 27 sections and 200,000 people a weekend, Saturday and Sunday only. Arrive at 09:00 with a list; by early afternoon the heat makes it hard work, and one section eats two hours.

places.name: Talat Noi
places.note: The oldest riverside settlement, Portuguese traders and a 1786 church, now machine-shop alleys, So Heng Tai Mansion and murals. The birthplace of kuaitiao khua kai; hours vary, check, and come late for the light.

places.name: Khao San Road
places.neighborhood: Banglamphu, 1km north of the Grand Palace
places.note: A 410m rice-market street from 1892, now bars, tailors and 40,000 backpackers a day in high season. Thirty minutes for the spectacle is plenty; hours vary, check, and skip it if drunk crowds are not your evening.

places.name: Lumphini Park
places.note: 57 hectares from 1925 with a 2.5km loop, 40 baht paddle boats and about 400 water monitors sunning by the lake. Go at dawn with the tai chi and the runners, or at dusk; no smoking anywhere in it.

places.name: Chao Phraya express boat
places.note: The orange-flag commuter boat, not a tour boat, past Wat Arun, the Grand Palace and Talat Noi's warehouses for under 50 baht. The cheapest sightseeing hour in the city; avoid rush hour, when it is standing room only.

places.name: Asiatique The Riverfront
places.note: Early-1900s East Asiatic Company warehouses turned into a riverside night market with a 60m Ferris wheel. Take the free shuttle boat from Sathorn pier, about every 15 to 20 minutes from 16:00 to 22:00, not a taxi.

places.name: Jay Fai
places.note: The only street stall with a Michelin star, held since 2018; Jay Fai cooks over charcoal in ski goggles. Order the crab omelette, over 1,000 baht; book well ahead, cash only, closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Thipsamai
places.neighborhood: Mahachai Road, Old City, a few doors from Jay Fai
places.note: Pad thai since the 1950s, on sun-dried Chanthaburi noodles and its own prawn oil. Order the pad thai wrapped in egg and a fresh orange juice; open until midnight, closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Krua Apsorn
places.note: A family-run Bib Gourmand with air conditioning and a royal following. Order the stir-fried crab with black pepper and the yellow curry with lotus root and prawns; cash only.

places.name: Rung Rueang Pork Noodle
places.note: A Bib Gourmand pork noodle shop that is a neighbourhood lunch, not a destination. Order the tom yum broth with the house fishballs; cash only, no bookings, and it shuts at 17:00.

places.name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu
places.note: Bib Gourmand pad thai over a hard flame. Get the char-grilled pork loin or the whole prawn in shell; open until midnight, so it is the late dinner after the Golden Mount.

places.name: Pae Brass Pot Porridge
places.note: Rice porridge cooked in brass pots by the same family since 1962, Bib Gourmand. Ask for the mixed-rice version the regulars order; cash only, and a breakfast on the way to Chatuchak.

places.name: Sky Bar at Lebua State Tower
places.note: The open-air rooftop from The Hangover Part II; cocktails run 600 to 700 baht and no shorts or sandals for men. Hours vary, check; arrive just before sunset for a spot at the rail.

places.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
places.neighborhood: Doi Suthep, 15km from the Old City
places.note: A 24m gold chedi said to hold part of the Buddha's shoulder bone, up 309 naga steps or a funicular. 120,000 people a month come, so be there at 06:00 and take the city view from the terrace.

places.name: Wat Chedi Luang
places.note: A 14th-century chedi that stood 82m until a 16th-century earthquake took the top off. Stay for the free daily Monk Chat, where you ask monks about Buddhism directly.

places.name: Wat Phra Singh
places.note: Founded 1345 and home to the Phra Buddha Sihing; the Viharn Lai Kham, 1815 to 1821, has some of the best Lanna murals in the city. Come early, before the Chedi Luang tour groups.

places.name: Wat Chiang Man
places.neighborhood: Old City, by the north wall
places.note: The oldest temple in the city, founded 1297 by King Mangrai, its chedi ringed by 15 stucco elephants. Free and usually empty; a 1581 stele here records the founding date of Chiang Mai itself.

places.name: Wat Umong
places.neighborhood: Foot of Doi Suthep, near Chiang Mai University
places.note: A forest temple from 1297 where you walk brick tunnels with faded murals to reach the chedi on top. The field of broken, discarded Buddhas by the pond is stranger than any temple in town; free.

places.name: Wat Suan Dok
places.neighborhood: Suthep Road, west of the Old City
places.note: A 48m Sri Lankan-style chedi from 1370, ringed by the white tombs of Chiang Mai's royal family. A working monastic university, free; come late afternoon, when the tombs catch the sunset.

places.name: Tha Phae Gate and the moat
places.neighborhood: East entrance to the Old City
places.note: The gate was rebuilt in 1985 to 1987 on the site of King Mangrai's 1296 original. Walk or cycle the moat loop in about 90 minutes and you pass all the Old City temples; hours vary, check.

places.name: Sunday Walking Street
places.neighborhood: Ratchadamnoen Road, from Tha Phae Gate
places.note: Sunday evenings only, the road shuts to traffic for northern food stalls and crafts, and Wat Phra Singh's courtyard becomes a food court. Shoulder to shoulder from 18:00 to 20:00; make it dinner.

places.name: Warorot Market
places.neighborhood: Chang Moi, by the Ping River
places.note: The biggest and oldest market in town, since 1910, where locals buy sai ua sausage, curry paste and dried goods, not souvenirs. Go in the morning, it thins by mid-afternoon; Guay Jub is round the corner.

places.name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar
places.note: Every night, not only weekends: crafts, portraits and clothes across several buildings and side streets. A souvenir market, not a food one; eat at Rasik Local Kitchen round the corner first.

places.name: Elephant Nature Park
places.note: A sanctuary founded in 1998 on 250 acres where you feed and bathe elephants and nobody rides them. Books out weeks ahead November to February; the price is about 85 dollars and hours vary, check with the park.

places.name: Doi Inthanon National Park
places.note: Thailand's highest point at 2,565m, a full day there and back. The usual stops are the Mae Klang, Wachirathan and Siriphum falls and the twin royal chedis; in September, the wettest month, the trails are slick.

places.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
places.neighborhood: Ratchaphruek Road, just north of the Old City
places.note: Bib Gourmand khao soi, curried egg noodles, in small bowls, so order two. Cash only and closed Sundays; a lunch, as it shuts at 16:00.

places.name: Huen Muan Jai
places.note: Northern Thai cooking in a wooden Lanna house with a garden, Bib Gourmand. Order the galangal dip with steamed mushrooms and the snakehead fish soup; closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Guay Jub Chang Moi Tat Mai
places.note: Bib Gourmand guay jub, peppery rolled-noodle soup, with sai ua, crispy pork and liver. Cash only; the natural lunch after a Warorot morning, and it closes at 15:00.

places.name: Rasik Local Kitchen
places.neighborhood: Sridonchai Road, by the Night Bazaar
places.note: A Bib Gourmand tasting menu for 14 to 16 people over three seatings, built on what the chef found that day. Book ahead, it is mandatory; closed Tuesdays, and the one splurge in town.

places.name: Lung Khajohn Wat Ket
places.neighborhood: Wat Ket, east bank of the Ping
places.note: A Bib Gourmand breakfast stall across the river from the tourist track. Order khao kriap pak mo, steamed rice dumplings in coconut milk, and the stuffed tapioca dumplings; cash only, closed Sundays.

places.name: Ao Nang beach and headland
places.note: The town beach under limestone headlands, more a longtail launch than a swim beach; the islands offshore have the better water. The strip behind it is where you eat and drink; hours vary, check.

places.name: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea)
places.neighborhood: Kiriwong Valley, north of Krabi Town
places.note: 1,260 steps, some risers over 30cm, climb 278m to a golden Buddha and a view over the karst. Start at 07:00 before the heat, and keep food out of sight: the monkeys on the lower steps take it from your hands.

places.name: Four Islands by longtail
places.note: Ko Poda, Ko Kai, Ko Mor and Chicken Island inside the national park; Ko Poda has the best sand and snorkelling. The big tour boats land by 11:00, so take an early or private longtail. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Krabi Town riverfront night market
places.neighborhood: Krabi Town, at the river mouth
places.note: The provincial capital's riverside night market, where the Krabi River meets Phang Nga Bay, and the local dinner scene, well away from the Ao Nang strip. Go hungry and graze.

places.name: Khao Phanom Bencha National Park
places.note: Rainforest round the 1,397m peak, with the five-tier Huai To Falls and Huai Sakhe Falls as the walks. Almost no tour buses, unlike the Emerald Pool; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ko Phi Phi Don and Maya Bay
places.neighborhood: Speedboat from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier
places.note: About an hour by speedboat. Tonsai on Phi Phi Don is bars and dive shops, not a swim beach; take the boat that also stops at Maya Bay, where it is one hour, no swimming, 2,000 people a day. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Susan Hoi shell cemetery
places.note: A 2km shoreline slab of fossil snail shells over 70 million years old, one of a handful of shell-fossil beaches anywhere. A 30 minute stop on the way to Krabi Town; hours vary, check.

places.name: Boat Noodle Ao Nang
places.note: Boat noodles in beef broth with morning glory for 80 baht a bowl, plus pad thai and oyster omelette. Cash only, plastic chairs, in and out in half an hour.

places.name: Krua Thara
places.neighborhood: Noppharat Thara, by the park pier
places.note: Seafood by the national park pier. Order the raw oysters, steamed cockles and grilled snapper, and the pak lieang greens if they have them; a taxi or scooter ride from central Ao Nang, not a walk.

places.name: A-One Restaurant
places.note: Candlelit Thai with a full cocktail bar, a step up from the beach stalls without resort prices. Most dishes start near 150 baht; the prawn, mussel and squid stir-fry is about 220.

places.name: Bussaba Thai Restaurant
places.note: Thai a step inland and uphill from the beach strip, and the date-night table the expats keep going back to. Worth the short walk off the beach road.

places.name: Azzurra
places.neighborhood: Ao Nang Road, west beach section
places.note: Italian with homemade pasta under Tuscan murals. Order the seafood tagliatelle; it is the midweek break from pad thai and grilled fish.

places.name: Carnivore Steak and Grill
places.note: Steaks on the same inland road as Bussaba, better than the grills on the beach road. Around 22 dollars a head, the priciest dinner on this list.

places.name: The Last Fisherman Bar
places.neighborhood: Southeast end of the beach walkway
places.note: The sunset bar at the quiet end of the beach walkway, with a Thai and Western menu that makes it dinner too. Walk down once the day-trip boats have gone.

places.name: Lae Lay Grill and The Hilltop
places.note: Two sea-view terraces on one hilltop, the nearest Ao Nang has to a sunset bar with food. You pay above beach-road prices for the view; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ao Nang Night Market
places.note: Grilled seafood, kebabs, pad thai and pork skewers with seats and live music. The dinner that needs no booking.

places.name: Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot)
places.neighborhood: Khlong Thom, Than Bok Khorani park
places.note: A spring pool with a real green tint, and the Blue Pool a short walk on. Roughly 60km from Ao Nang, so it is the day; swimming is closed in some seasons, so check before you drive.

places.name: Hat Noppharat Thara
places.neighborhood: West end of Ao Nang, park headquarters
places.note: The calmer, longer beach next door, backed by casuarinas and the park visitor centre, with a quieter boat pier than Ao Nang's front. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Railay West Beach
places.note: The swimmable, sunset side of a peninsula with no road in. Of its four zones (West, East, Phra Nang, Ton Sai) this is the resort one; no boats after dark, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Phra Nang Cave and Beach
places.note: The most photographed beach of the group and a princess fertility shrine in the cave, reached by the public boardwalk under the cliffs from East Railay. Early, before the boats; hours vary, check.

places.name: Thaiwand Wall climbing
places.neighborhood: East Railay and Ton Sai cliffs
places.note: The limestone that made Railay a climbing destination: half-day taster courses and multi-pitch routes from the shops on East Railay. Hours vary, check with the shop.

places.name: Ton Sai Beach
places.neighborhood: Ton Sai, northwest of Railay West
places.note: The scruffier, cheaper climbers' corner, over a rock path from Railay West at low tide or by its own boat. The evening is here, campfire bars and slacklines, not on Railay West; hours vary, check.

places.name: The Grotto at Rayavadee
places.note: Rayavadee's restaurant under a real limestone overhang, one of the resort's four dining rooms and the splurge on the peninsula. Confirm they seat non-guests before you walk over; hours vary, check.

places.name: Kohinoor Indian Restaurant
places.note: British-style Indian on the walking street: tandoori, vindaloo, saag paneer. The night you need a break from Thai food.

places.name: Mom's Kitchen
places.note: A local kitchen on the mangrove side, not a resort restaurant. Order the panang curry with squid or the garlic-pepper seafood, under 100 baht a dish.

places.name: Phra Nang Cuisine
places.neighborhood: Railay East, next to Mom's Kitchen
places.note: Fresh coffee on floor cushions on a deck by the water. A slow morning before the tide lets you walk round to Phra Nang; hours vary, check.

places.name: Mama Chicken
places.note: Grilled chicken, som tam and sticky rice for under 80 baht from a stall on the jungle trail. The climbers eat here from breakfast to dinner.

places.name: Maxi
places.note: Massaman and other curries from paste pounded by hand, in the climbers' corner. Pair it with the low-tide walk over; hours vary, check.

places.name: Skunk House
places.note: A two-floor reggae bar with a Thai singer most nights. The walkable night out if you sleep on the sunset side.

places.name: The Last Bar
places.note: Fire spinning, a muay Thai ring, pool tables and a dance floor. Open from breakfast to 02:00, and the only late night on the peninsula.

places.name: Tew Lay Bar
places.neighborhood: Far east end of Railay East
places.note: Hammocks and cushions over the water, coffee by day and cocktails by night. The quiet end of Railay East, away from The Last Bar.

places.name: Diamond Cave and Railay Viewpoint
places.neighborhood: Inland trail, Railay East to Phra Nang
places.note: A steep scramble on ropes and roots to a lookout over both beaches, past a stalactite cave. Not a stroll: shoes with grip, and skip it after rain.

places.name: Princess Lagoon
places.note: A rope scramble to a lagoon walled in by limestone, swimmable only a couple of hours either side of low tide. Read the tide table first; the ropes are dangerous wet, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Deep-water solo climbing
places.neighborhood: Boat-access cliffs off Phra Nang and Ton Sai
places.note: Half a day by longtail to climb overhanging limestone with the sea as the crash pad, no rope, no harness. Book at the shops that run the Thaiwand courses; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ton Sai to Railay low-tide walk
places.neighborhood: Headland path, Ton Sai to Railay West
places.note: The free way between Ton Sai and Railay West, a rock scramble over the headland that opens only at low tide. Check the tide or you pay for the boat back anyway; hours vary, check.

places.name: Mu Ko Lanta National Park and Ko Rok
places.neighborhood: Southern tip and the outer islands
places.note: 134 sq km from 1990: the south tip of Lanta plus Ko Rok and the other islands by speedboat. The islands close every year from 16 May to 31 October, no exceptions; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ko Lanta Old Town
places.neighborhood: East coast of Ko Lanta Yai
places.note: The first settlement, stilt houses and wooden shophouses on the calm east coast, and a different island from the west-coast resorts. Lunch at Apsara, a beer at Big Tree; hours vary, check.

places.name: Time for Lime cooking school
places.note: A beachfront cooking school of 23-plus years whose profits fund Lanta Animal Welfare next door; the rescue dogs wander the kitchen. Classes at 11:00 and 17:00, about 5 hours; book by WhatsApp and ring the bell at the gate.

places.name: Laanta Seafood
places.neighborhood: Baan Saladan, west of the pier
places.note: Southern Thai seafood in big portions, dishes under 50 baht, by the pier where the boats come in. Cash, plastic chairs, no view, fresh catch.

places.name: The Table
places.neighborhood: Baan Saladan, off the main drag
places.note: A reservation-only Thai tasting menu with every guest at one table, Monday to Saturday. Book ahead; the one splurge on Lanta that is not a resort dining room.

places.name: Krua Lanta Yai
places.note: Thai seafood on stilted terraces over the mangroves. The east-coast alternative to the west-beach restaurants; pair it with an Old Town afternoon.

places.name: Apsara Restaurant
places.note: Grilled fish with a choice of eight sauces among Old Town's wooden shophouses. The lunch stop on the Old Town walk; closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Salty Fish Beach Bistro
places.note: A more careful Thai beach dinner than the plastic-chair standard, on Khlong Tob between the Phra Ae and Khlong Nin strips. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Sang Ga U Seafood
places.note: Floating restaurants on the fish farms of the Urak Lawoi (Chao Ley) village: order what is in the pen below you. A scooter or taxi ride; ask here about the full-moon boat ceremonies.

places.name: Nang Sabai German Bakery
places.note: The German-run bakery on Khlong Dao: homemade bread and cakes, and breakfast for everyone staying on that beach. Shuts at 17:00, so never dinner.

places.name: Big Tree Beer Garden
places.note: Thai craft beer in the middle of Old Town; order the Chalawan Pale Ale. The stop that breaks up the shophouse walk.

places.name: The Fat Monkey (Ling Uan)
places.note: Cocktails and pizza under a sign reading Crap Food and Warm Beer, which undersells it. The sundowner before Khlong Dao's restaurant row fills up.

places.name: Khlong Dao Beach
places.note: The calmest swimming on the island and the most resorts, a walk from Saladan for the pier and the Wednesday and Saturday market. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Haad Phra Ae (Long Beach)
places.neighborhood: West coast, south of Khlong Dao
places.note: The longest beach on Lanta: package resorts at one end, the old hippie bars (Happy, Irie, Gypsy, Treehouse) at the north tip. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Khlong Nin Beach
places.note: Quieter than Khlong Dao, with a short row of beach bars (Horizon, Otto, Rasta Baby) instead of a resort strip. Lanta's beach without Lanta's crowds; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ao Kantiang Beach
places.neighborhood: Far south of Ko Lanta Yai
places.note: The last real beach before the park tip, under a limestone headland. Pimalai Resort's dining rooms take non-guests for one dressed-up night; hours vary, check.

places.name: Saladan pier and market
places.note: The arrival town for the Krabi transfer and a stop on the island's rotating market, here Wednesdays and Saturdays, for southern curries and khao mok gai. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Laem Tanod lighthouse
places.neighborhood: Southern tip, inside the national park
places.note: A short walk from the park gate to a lighthouse on the headland, looking out over the outer islands. The land half of a Ko Rok day, if you do not want all of it on the water.

places.name: Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha)
places.note: A 12m gold Buddha from 1972 on an islet joined by a causeway, up a naga staircase lined with amulet stalls. Pair it with Wat Plai Laem and lunch on Bang Rak; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ang Thong National Marine Park
places.note: 42 limestone islands with inland marine lakes, a Ramsar site since 2002 and the karst from The Beach. Authorised tour boats only; park fee 25 to 300 baht plus the boat, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Chaweng Beach
places.note: Samui's first and biggest tourist strip, the busiest beach and the nightlife. Sleep in Bophut and come here for Ark Bar; hours vary, check.

places.name: Lamai Beach
places.note: The second strip after Chaweng, a little quieter and more local but still resort country. Beach Republic is at the north end; hours vary, check.

places.name: Fisherman's Village Walking Street
places.note: Friday nights only, the old Chinese-Thai fishing village's front becomes a walking street through converted shophouses. The most walkable dinner on the island; hours vary, check.

places.name: Na Muang Waterfalls
places.note: Two jungle falls: Na Muang 1, and Na Muang 2 up a longer uphill walk to a taller drop. Free, and one of the few things to do inland; hours vary, check.

places.name: Fisherman's House Cafe
places.note: Brunch and northern Thai coffee in a restored wooden shophouse, breakfast plates over 200 baht. The polished end of Fisherman's Village.

places.name: The Shack Bar & Grill
places.note: Australian-American steaks, ribs and burgers, dinner only. A full rack or a steak is over 1,000 baht; the counterpoint to the seafood up and down the lane.

places.name: The Hut
places.neighborhood: East end of the village lane
places.note: Thai seafood and stir-fries at the quiet end of the lane. Grilled seafood about 300 baht, curries and stir-fries nearer 100.

places.name: Zazen Restaurant
places.note: French and Italian with a Thai menu and a morning high tea, in a resort dining room. The dressed-up dinner in Bophut; hours vary, check.

places.name: Red Moon
places.note: French-run, with tapas, Australian steaks and Thai on one menu. The group dinner when nobody agrees; hours vary, check.

places.name: Ark Bar Beach Club
places.note: Twenty-plus years on Chaweng sand: two pools, pool parties 14:00 to 19:00, beach parties 20:00 to 02:00. Free entry after 14:00; come for the 20:00 fire show, not the daytime pool.

places.name: Beach Republic
places.note: An infinity pool over the beach with Thai food, Angus burgers and a newer Mexican menu. The calmer, design-led answer to Ark Bar, just past Soi Renaissance coming from Chaweng.

places.name: Talad Sod Bophut
places.neighborhood: Ring road, across from Soi Sundays
places.note: The morning market Bophut actually shops at, dishes around 40 baht. Breakfast, not dinner; it has packed up long before the Friday walking street sets up.

places.name: Wat Plai Laem
places.neighborhood: Bang Rak, near the Big Buddha
places.note: An 18-armed Guanyin over a lily pond beside a laughing Buddha, five minutes from the Big Buddha. Free, and quieter than its neighbour.

places.name: Secret Buddha Garden
places.note: A hillside of stone statues a farmer began in 1976, strange rather than manicured, up a rough road that needs a car or a strong scooter. Do it with Na Muang, same inland detour.

places.name: The Frog & Gecko
places.note: Pub food, draft beer, quiz nights and a sea view. The quiet alternative to the Friday walking street crowd; hours vary, check.
